children: Shares of Fluence Energy slid after the company cut its full-year outlook, citing delays at its contract manufacturing facility.
The stock fell 20% to $7.21 in premarket trading on Thursday. At Wednesday's market close, shares were down 54% year to date.
The battery energy storage system provider said Wednesday that it now expects annual sales to be $2.4 billion at the midpoint, down from its previous guidance of $3 billion.
Its adjusted loss before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization is now projected to be $200 million, compared with the previously forecasted loss of $10 million.

While demand has remained strong, Fluence's plans to ramp up its contract manufacturing site in Houston has been slowed, Chief Executive Julian Nebreda said. Fluence is taking additional steps to restructure its organization and streamline planning across the supply chain and manufacturing. Its contract manufacturer has implemented corrective actions that have already increased daily production levels, Nebreda said.
Analysts said the production delays add to questions around the company's execution in the past few years.
"We view the announcement as another hit to confidence in execution, which was already thin," Truist Securities analysts said in a note.
